doc: Q306: data/anatomy/concepts_q306.json -- the CONCEPT layer of the search. A clinician types things that are not structures: "pelvic tilt", "impingement", "compartment syndrome", "carpal tunnel", "Q angle", "pennation". Before Q306 the search had no concept layer at all: 39 of the 42 clinical concepts in the Q306 reference list returned nothing on every page, measured in docs/research/Q306_search_coverage_audit.md. Each concept names the STRUCTURES and the GROUPS the pages already carry, and every biomechanical claim carries its own citation. `offer_structures` are targets resolved against each page's own names at build time by scripts/anatomy/q298/build_search_q298.py (same three rules as a synonym entry), `offer_groups` are group ids from data/anatomy/{muscle_groups_q283.json, relations_q298.json, groups_q306.json}, and `sim` names a Q283 pose-rig degree of freedom where the concept has one, so the card can link the action simulation. A concept that is a DIAGNOSIS rather than an anatomical fact says so and offers the structures involved without asserting a mechanism.

kinds.concept: An anatomical or biomechanical concept that is not a structure.
kinds.region: A named space, canal, fossa or tunnel bounded by structures the pages ship.
kinds.measure: A measurement or descriptor; says whether this project computes it and from what.
kinds.diagnosis: A clinical diagnosis. The atlas shows the anatomy and asserts no mechanism.
kinds.posture: An alignment descriptor. No normative value is shipped.

he_note: HEBREW IS A PROJECT-SUPPLIED TRANSLATION, NOT A PUBLISHED TERMINOLOGY -- the same declaration data/anatomy/synonyms_q298.json carries in sources.he.

concepts.label: Pelvic tilt
concepts.body: Pelvic tilt is the orientation of the pelvis, not a structure. It is described in three planes: ANTERIOR / POSTERIOR tilt in the sagittal plane and LATERAL tilt (pelvic obliquity, 'pelvic drop') in the frontal plane. Pick one of the three below to see the muscles that produce it on this page.
concepts.note: The three tilts are the standard clinical description; each has its own entry with its own sources.

concepts.label: Anterior pelvic tilt
concepts.body: The pelvis rotates forward about the hip joints, so the ASIS moves below the PSIS and lumbar lordosis tends to increase. Produced / maintained by the HIP FLEXORS in front and the lumbar extensors behind.

claims.text: Stretching the hip flexors reduced anterior pelvic tilt: "a mean increase of 2.6 deg in passive hip extension and a corresponding mean reduction of 1.2 deg in anterior pelvic tilt" (P < .001).
The lumbar multifidus is more active in anterior than in posterior pelvic tilt: "MF muscle activity during the exercise involving PPT was significantly lower than that involving APT".
The hip flexor group named by this project's own cited action data is the iliopsoas (psoas major and iliacus), rectus femoris, sartorius and adductor longus.

concepts.label: Posterior pelvic tilt
concepts.body: The pelvis rotates backward about the hip joints, so the ASIS moves above the PSIS and lumbar lordosis tends to flatten. Produced by the HIP EXTENSORS (gluteus maximus, hamstrings) and the ABDOMINAL WALL.

claims.text: Gluteus maximus is more active in posterior pelvic tilt than in anterior or neutral: "GM muscle activity during the exercise involving PPT was significantly higher than that involving APT and NPT".
Abdominal contraction shifts the pelvis and unloads the back extensors: it "increased external oblique muscle activity, reduced erector spinae and multifidus muscles activity".
"The hamstring muscles may play an important role in achieving pelvic balance during the lifting maneuver."

concepts.label: Lateral pelvic tilt (pelvic obliquity)
concepts.body: One side of the pelvis drops relative to the other in the frontal plane. In single-leg stance the STANCE-side hip abductors hold the pelvis level; when they fail, the opposite (swing) side drops. The quadratus lumborum acts on the pelvis from above.

claims.text: Weaker hip abductors go with a greater drop of the opposite side of the pelvis: runners who developed medial tibial stress syndrome had "weaker hip abductors (P = 0.008)" and "greater contralateral pelvic drop (P = 0.021)".

Reducing the drop goes with earlier and longer gluteus medius activity: "peak contralateral pelvic drop ... were reduced after retraining", accompanied by "earlier activation of the gluteus medius relative to foot strike" and "longer duration of gluteus medius activity".
Abdominal bracing reduces pelvic obliquity during lifting: it "decreased pelvis obliquity angle in both groups".

concepts.label: Carpal tunnel
concepts.body: The space between the carpal arch and the flexor retinaculum. Its contents on this page are offered below. Carpal tunnel syndrome is a median-nerve compression DIAGNOSIS, not a structure; the atlas shows the anatomy, not the diagnosis.

claims.text: The flexor retinaculum of the hand is the transverse carpal ligament; the tunnel's contents are the four FDP and four FDS tendons, the FPL tendon and the median nerve.

concepts.label: Cubital tunnel
concepts.body: The passage of the ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle of the humerus. Its boundaries are bone and retinaculum, not a mesh of their own.

claims.text: The ulnar nerve passes behind the medial epicondyle of the humerus and enters the forearm between the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris.

concepts.label: Tarsal tunnel
concepts.body: Behind the medial malleolus, deep to the flexor retinaculum of the ankle: the tibial nerve, the posterior tibial vessels and the tendons of tibialis posterior, FDL and FHL.

claims.text: The structures behind the medial malleolus, from front to back, are the tendon of tibialis posterior, the tendon of flexor digitorum longus, the posterior tibial artery and vein, the tibial nerve and the tendon of flexor hallucis longus.

concepts.label: Guyon's canal (ulnar canal of the wrist)
concepts.body: The passage of the ulnar nerve and artery at the wrist, between the pisiform and the hook of the hamate. An eponymous space, not a mesh.

claims.text: The ulnar nerve and artery enter the hand superficial to the flexor retinaculum, between the pisiform and the hook of the hamate.

concepts.label: Adductor canal (Hunter's canal, subsartorial canal)
concepts.body: An intermuscular space in the middle third of the medial thigh carrying the femoral artery and vein and the saphenous nerve, roofed by sartorius; it ends at the adductor hiatus in adductor magnus.

claims.text: The adductor canal is bounded by vastus medialis, adductor longus and adductor magnus, roofed by sartorius, and transmits the femoral artery and vein and the saphenous nerve; the femoral artery leaves it through the adductor hiatus to become the popliteal artery.

concepts.label: Popliteal fossa
concepts.body: The diamond behind the knee: hamstrings above, the two heads of gastrocnemius below, carrying the tibial and common fibular nerves and the popliteal vessels.

claims.text: The popliteal fossa is bounded above by biceps femoris laterally and semitendinosus and semimembranosus medially, and below by the two heads of gastrocnemius.

concepts.label: Cubital fossa
concepts.body: The triangle in front of the elbow, carrying the biceps tendon, the brachial artery and the median nerve from lateral to medial.

claims.text: The cubital fossa is bounded laterally by brachioradialis and medially by pronator teres; its contents from lateral to medial are the biceps tendon, the brachial artery and the median nerve.

concepts.label: Femoral triangle
concepts.body: In the upper medial thigh: inguinal ligament above, sartorius laterally, adductor longus medially, carrying the femoral nerve, artery and vein.

claims.text: The femoral triangle is bounded by the inguinal ligament, the medial border of sartorius and the medial border of adductor longus; its floor is iliopsoas and pectineus.

concepts.label: Anatomical snuffbox
concepts.body: The hollow on the radial side of the wrist, floored by the scaphoid and the trapezium, with the radial artery crossing it.

claims.text: The anatomical snuffbox is bounded in front by the tendons of abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis and behind by the tendon of extensor pollicis longus; its floor is the scaphoid and the trapezium, crossed by the radial artery.

concepts.label: Axilla
concepts.body: The pyramidal space between the arm and the chest wall, carrying the axillary artery and vein and the brachial plexus.

claims.text: The anterior wall of the axilla is pectoralis major and pectoralis minor, the posterior wall is subscapularis, teres major and latissimus dorsi, and the medial wall is serratus anterior over the ribs.

concepts.label: Inguinal canal
concepts.body: An oblique passage through the anterior abdominal wall above the inguinal ligament. Hernia is a DIAGNOSIS, not a structure; the atlas shows the wall.

claims.text: The inguinal canal lies above the medial half of the inguinal ligament; its anterior wall is the aponeurosis of external oblique and its floor is the inguinal ligament.

concepts.label: Greater sciatic foramen
concepts.body: The gap between the sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments and the hip bone, divided by piriformis; the sciatic nerve and the gluteal vessels and nerves pass through it. Piriformis syndrome is a DIAGNOSIS; the atlas shows the anatomy.

claims.text: Piriformis passes through the greater sciatic foramen and divides it; the sciatic nerve usually leaves the pelvis below piriformis.

concepts.label: Thoracic outlet
concepts.body: The passage of the brachial plexus and the subclavian vessels between the scalene muscles, the first rib and the clavicle. Thoracic outlet syndrome is a DIAGNOSIS; the atlas shows the passage.

claims.text: The brachial plexus and the subclavian artery pass between the anterior and middle scalene muscles over the first rib; the subclavian vein passes in front of the anterior scalene.

concepts.label: Pennation angle
concepts.body: The angle between a muscle's fibres and its line of pull. This project measures and ships fibre direction per muscle part (Q289) and the ultrasound architecture table (data/anatomy/us_architecture_q289.json); pick a muscle to see its own figures on its card.

claims.text: This project's own fibre-direction and architecture data is in data/anatomy/us_architecture_q289.json (Q289) and is shown per muscle part on the card; it is not re-derived here.

concepts.label: Range of motion (ROM)
concepts.body: The angular range a joint can move through. This project's pose rig (data/anatomy/pose_rig_<page>.json, Q241) carries a limit per degree of freedom, and the Q283 action simulation moves within it; pick a joint or a muscle to see the degrees of freedom it crosses.

claims.text: The limits the simulation obeys are this project's own pose-rig limits per degree of freedom (data/anatomy/pose_rig_*.json), not a published normative range: no normative ROM table is shipped.

concepts.note: No normative ROM values are claimed. The rig's limits are a modelling choice of this project.

concepts.label: Moment arm / line of action
concepts.body: The perpendicular distance from a muscle's line of pull to the joint axis. This project COMPUTES it for every muscle about every pose-rig joint it crosses, from each page's own meshes (Q284), and badges it as computed on the Learn card.

claims.text: The moment arms shown are computed from each page's own geometry about its own pose-rig joints (data/anatomy/moment_arms_<page>.json, Q284) and are badged as computed, not cited.

concepts.label: Q angle
concepts.body: The angle between the pull of quadriceps and the patellar ligament, measured from the ASIS through the patella to the tibial tuberosity. This project ships the bones and the muscles it is measured on, but NO Q-angle value: the three landmarks are not shipped as meshes.

claims.text: No Q-angle figure is computed or claimed here. The ASIS and the tibial tuberosity are bone LANDMARKS and this project ships no mesh for either, which is the same reason ASIS and AIIS return an explanation rather than a structure.

concepts.note: Stated as a gap, not a measurement.

concepts.label: Compartments and compartment syndrome
concepts.body: A compartment is a group of muscles enclosed by deep fascia and bone. Compartment syndrome is a DIAGNOSIS (pressure inside a compartment), not a structure: the atlas shows the compartments and the fascia that bound them. The compartments this project has cited membership for are offered below.

claims.text: The compartments with cited membership in this project are the anterior and the lateral compartment of the leg (data/anatomy/muscle_groups_q283.json, Gray's 4th ed.). The remaining compartments of the leg, thigh, forearm, hand and foot have no cited membership data here yet, and the search says so rather than offering a guess.

concepts.note: Honest partial answer: 2 of the standard compartments have cited membership, the rest do not.

concepts.label: Subacromial impingement
concepts.body: Pain attributed to the space between the acromion and the humeral head. The structures of that space on this page are offered below.

claims.text: The supraspinatus tendon and the subacromial bursa lie between the acromion and the head of the humerus.
No page ships a coracoacromial ligament mesh, so the roof of the space is shown by the scapula's acromion and coracoid process only; this is a gap, stated rather than filled.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI)
concepts.body: Contact between the femoral head-neck junction and the acetabular rim.

claims.text: The acetabular labrum is attached to the margin of the acetabulum and is continuous with the transverse acetabular ligament.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: Plantar fasciitis / plantar heel pain
concepts.body: Pain at the attachment of the plantar aponeurosis to the calcaneus.

claims.text: The plantar aponeurosis is attached posteriorly to the calcaneal tuberosity and divides distally into bands for the toes.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow)
concepts.body: Pain at the common extensor origin on the lateral epicondyle of the humerus.

claims.text: The superficial extensors of the forearm arise from a common tendon on the lateral epicondyle of the humerus.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: Medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow)
concepts.body: Pain at the common flexor origin on the medial epicondyle of the humerus.

claims.text: The superficial flexors of the forearm arise from a common tendon on the medial epicondyle of the humerus.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: Adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder)
concepts.body: Painful loss of glenohumeral motion attributed to the joint capsule.

claims.text: The glenohumeral joint capsule is attached to the margin of the glenoid cavity and to the anatomical neck of the humerus.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: Medial tibial stress syndrome (shin splints)
concepts.body: Exercise-related pain along the medial border of the tibia.

claims.text: Runners who developed medial tibial stress syndrome had "tighter iliotibial bands", "weaker hip abductors" and "greater contralateral pelvic drop" than those who did not.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: Popliteal (Baker's) cyst
concepts.body: A distended bursa behind the knee, classically between the medial head of gastrocnemius and semimembranosus.

claims.text: A subtendinous bursa lies between the medial head of gastrocnemius and the capsule of the knee joint, and may communicate with the joint cavity.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: De Quervain's tenosynovitis
concepts.body: Pain at the first dorsal compartment of the wrist, where APL and EPB share a sheath.

claims.text: The first compartment under the extensor retinaculum transmits the tendons of abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: Piriformis syndrome / deep gluteal syndrome
concepts.body: Sciatic symptoms attributed to the deep gluteal space rather than to the lumbar spine.

claims.text: The sciatic nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, usually below piriformis.

concepts.note: A DIAGNOSIS, not a structure. The atlas shows the anatomy involved and asserts no mechanism, severity or treatment.

concepts.label: Lumbar lordosis
concepts.body: The forward curve of the lumbar spine in the sagittal plane. Related to pelvic tilt: see 'anterior pelvic tilt'.

claims.text: The atlas shows this body's own geometry; no normative or diagnostic figure is claimed.

concepts.note: A descriptor of alignment, not a structure. No normative value is shipped.

concepts.label: Thoracic kyphosis
concepts.body: The backward curve of the thoracic spine in the sagittal plane.

claims.text: The atlas shows this body's own geometry; no normative or diagnostic figure is claimed.

concepts.note: A descriptor of alignment, not a structure. No normative value is shipped.

concepts.label: Scoliosis
concepts.body: A lateral curvature of the spine with rotation. The atlas ships a Cobb-angle MEASURING tool (Q294); it does not diagnose and ships no scoliotic spine.

claims.text: The atlas shows this body's own geometry; no normative or diagnostic figure is claimed.

concepts.note: A descriptor of alignment, not a structure. No normative value is shipped.

concepts.label: Genu valgum (knock knee)
concepts.body: A frontal-plane alignment of the knee. The atlas ships this body's own bones and no normative alignment figure.

claims.text: The atlas shows this body's own geometry; no normative or diagnostic figure is claimed.

concepts.note: A descriptor of alignment, not a structure. No normative value is shipped.

concepts.label: Genu varum (bow leg)
concepts.body: A frontal-plane alignment of the knee. The atlas ships this body's own bones and no normative alignment figure.

claims.text: The atlas shows this body's own geometry; no normative or diagnostic figure is claimed.

concepts.note: A descriptor of alignment, not a structure. No normative value is shipped.

concepts.label: Pes planus (flat foot) / pes cavus
concepts.body: The height of the longitudinal arch of the foot. The atlas ships the arch's own bones, ligaments and tendons and no normative arch figure.

claims.text: The atlas shows this body's own geometry; no normative or diagnostic figure is claimed.

concepts.note: A descriptor of alignment, not a structure. No normative value is shipped.
